title: Senior Actuarial Analyst
description:
About the Role
Location: Fully remote within the continental United States.
Use of AI data in insurance pricing entails regulatory review by state departments of insurance. When a carrier intends to use Nearmap data in its rates, both the carrier’s own actuaries and state insurance regulators can come back with various questions and/or objections. Many are predictable and specific: how was ground truth for an attribute determined, what do the goodness-of-fit metrics look like on held-out data? Others have never been asked before and have yet to be fully answered.
You will be the actuarial voice inside Nearmap ’s and our customers’ rate filings. Working with our AI and Computer Vision team, you will build a library of validation materials behind every Nearmap attribute and score used in rating, produce exhibits and memos for state DOI review, and answer regulator objections with analysis that holds up under scrutiny.
This is a customer-facing actuarial role, not a back-office one. You will report into Insurance Product and work alongside our regulatory affairs owner, who owns regulator relationships and submission mechanics, so your time goes to the analysis and the defense of it.
Key Responsibilities
You’ll own and defend the filing evidence:

• Coordinate on and collaborate with cross functional teams to produce the filing materials for each Nearmap attribute and score used in rating: model memos, validation and accuracy metrics, and the actuarial exhibits that go into a submission.

• Document and maintain what each state requires for model validation, including details on state-by-state confidentiality and trade secret treatments, ensuring Nearmap consistently produces exhibits that satisfies the NAIC checklist for model filings

• Turn model outputs into the evidence that filings need, such as model validation metrics, coverage rates, distributional analysis, bias and fairness testing, and by-state breakdowns. Lead the analytical response to regulator objections, working with our regulatory affairs owner on strategy, framing, and submission, and join calls with departments of insurance to explain methodology and results directly.

• Manage administration of Nearmap ’s filings including creating and maintaining SERFF accounts and keeping good records of all Nearmap filing materials and exchanges.

You'll work directly with customers:

• Advise on which attributes are filing-ready and which carry approval risk and build supporting materials to enable the GTM teams and customers ahead of time.

• Partner with carrier actuarial and pricing teams on how Nearmap data is best implemented in their rating plans.

• Collaborate with pre-sales to support data tests and lift analyses that demonstrate predictive value and help turn the results into something a filing can use.

You'll make the next filing cheaper than the last:

• Build reusable validation templates and exhibits so each new carrier program costs less effort than the one before it.

• Establish product requirements for new products and scores before they ship that makes them “filing ready” immediately upon release.

Experience

• 5+ years of property and casualty actuarial experience, with real exposure to pricing, ratemaking, or rate filings.

• ACAS or FCAS credentialing strongly preferred for this role. Candidates with substantial ratemaking and filing experience will be considered.

• Experience preparing actuarial exhibits for rate filings and responding to regulator objections.

• Bachelor's degree in actuarial science, statistics, mathematics, economics, or a related field.

• You can explain carrier-led rate filing processes to someone who is not an actuary without making them feel lost.

An agent can decide. An agent cannot be liable. Every hiring agent being built right now needs a deterministic, auditable layer underneath it. Build the engine. Extend the ontology, the policy engine and the automations framework. Make agents first-class callers through our APIs and MCP server.
Build the agent that writes configuration. Turn a policy, a union contract or a customer request into config a human reviews and ships. This is how a small team serves a big market.
Deploy into the field. Embed with customers and partners and build their compliance workflows as code. Everyone here gets close to the people who use what we build.
Grow the ecosystem. Open doors with the hiring platforms, staffing systems and HR software companies that distribute Onboarded, and turn signed partnerships into live customers.
Tell the story. Define a category in public. Write, ship, film and teach how the work that has to be right gets done in the agent era.

title: Regional Field Operations Manager
description:
About Quartermaster

Quartermaster is building the world's most comprehensive maritime intelligence platform. Our SmartMast™ system transforms commercial and civilian vessels into a persistent, distributed sensing network-combining HD video, AI, radar, RF sensing, and AIS to deliver real-time maritime domain awareness at global scale. With 600+ sensors deployed across 25+ countries and more than 400,000 vessels identified outside of AIS, we are setting a new standard for what ocean surveillance and safety can look like.

We are a startup in build mode: small team, high ownership, fast iteration, and meaningful constraints. We ship quickly, learn in production, and optimize for mission impact over process theater.

The Role

As Regional Field Operations Manager, you will own the deployment and performance of SmartMast™ across your region. Once Launch has opened a market and secured vessel partners, you turn those agreements into units that are installed, activated, and reporting, and you keep them reporting. Success is measured in units installed on schedule, uptime across the regional fleet, and the speed and quality of every install and repair.

You will build and run the regional field operation: technicians, installers, logistics, and spares. You will work hand in hand with the regional Head of Launch and report to Quartermaster's Field Operations leadership in the United States.

What You'll Own

- Deployment: Plan and execute SmartMast™ installations across the region's vessel partners, from vessel survey and scheduling through install, activation, and first data. Hit the deployment targets set with Launch and leadership.

- Fleet uptime: Keep every installed unit online and reporting. Own preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs, and unit swaps against clear response-time standards.

- Field team: Recruit, train, and lead regional field technicians and coordinators. Set the bar for install quality, safety, and professionalism aboard vessels.

- Logistics and inventory: Run in-country hardware flow, including receiving, warehousing, spares, staging, and reverse logistics for failed units, within the import framework Launch establishes.

- Vendor and installer management: Direct the local installers, fabricators, and port-side vendors that Launch onboards. Schedule their work, audit quality, and escalate or replace underperformers.

- Vessel and port coordination: Work with fleet operations teams, crews, and port staff to get aboard during short windows, around vessel schedules, port calls, and access rules.

- Field data and feedback: Track install, uptime, and repair metrics. Feed hardware and install issues back to engineering, and surface field realities to Launch and leadership.

- Process: Build repeatable install and maintenance procedures, safety practices, and documentation that scale across countries.

What You Need

- Experience: 6+ years in field operations, field service, or technical deployment, including at least 3 years leading field teams. Maritime, offshore, telecoms, or marine electronics strongly preferred.

- Deployment track record: Proven delivery of hardware rollouts across multiple sites or countries, on schedule and to quality standards.

- Hands-on technical depth: Comfort with vessel-installed electronics, including mounting, power, cabling, networking, and RF/antenna work. You can step aboard and troubleshoot alongside your team.

- Logistics instinct: Inventory and spares planning, customs-ready shipping, and getting parts to a vessel during a short port call.

- Safety: Working knowledge of shipboard safety practice and port access procedures in the region.

- Location: Based in the region and ready to travel up to 50% to ports and vessels, sometimes on short notice.

- Autonomy: Comfortable running an operation with leadership several time zones away.

- Language: Fluent professional English, plus the primary working languages of the region's ports and crews.
